claims.text: The conventionally processed NbMoTaW-based baseline is a homogeneous single-phase solid solution without engineered secondary dispersoids.
Controlled thermomechanical processing can produce a uniform dispersion of less than 1 vol% Y2O3 particles with sizes of 5–20 nm in a NbMoTaW-based alloy.
The introduced Y2O3 particles will be distributed both within the matrix and along grain boundaries.
Y2O3 nanoparticles impede dislocation motion at high temperature by acting as pinning sites.
Y2O3 nanoparticles impede grain-boundary sliding at high temperature.
A thermally stable strengthening microstructure can support elevated-temperature tensile strength and creep resistance in a high-entropy alloy.
The oxide-dispersed NbMoTaW-based alloy will have approximately 20–30% higher yield strength at about 900°C than the conventionally processed baseline.
The oxide-dispersed NbMoTaW-based alloy will have approximately 20–30% better creep resistance at about 900°C than the conventionally processed baseline.
The oxide dispersion will not significantly degrade room-temperature ductility or strength.
Keeping the Y2O3 content below 1 vol% will minimize the intervention's effect on alloy density.
Uniform and stable particle dispersion is required for the proposed high-temperature improvement.
Particle agglomeration may eliminate the high-temperature benefit or compromise low-temperature properties.
The estimated 20–30% improvement is inferred from analogous oxide-dispersion strengthening in Ni-based systems.
Some refractory high-entropy alloys combine high strength at or above 1000°C with room-temperature tensile ductility.
